quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
Ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: How do you stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the front brake first.
Slow the engine and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When adjusting mirrors, what should you focus on?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
Your arms.
The road in front of your motorcycle.
The side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely to allow for movement.
Hold the handgrips firmly to maintain control.
Use lots of throttle to help you over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet because it could become loose and cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to maintain control.
questions.explanation: When riding over a rough surface, hold the handgrips firmly to keep control of your motorcycle's direction.

questions.question: What percentage of a motorcycle's stopping power does the front brake supply?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
100 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should a face shield do?

options.text: Allow a clear view to both sides.
Prevent air from passing through it.
Be tight enough to prevent glasses from fitting underneath it.
Not fasten too tightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be free of scratches, resist penetration, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, permit air to pass through, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located?

options.text: By the left handgrip
By the right handgrip
By the left footrest
By the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: By the left handgrip
questions.explanation: Learn the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you start riding. The horn button is usually located next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Maintain your usual space cushion.
Brake later than usual.
Ride a little more slowly than usual.
Ride a little faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle sits lower with a passenger's weight. Ride a bit more slowly than usual, especially in curves and over bumps. The extra weight means your motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, or stop, so keep a larger space cushion.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Always use both brakes.
Only use the front brake.
Only use the rear brake on slippery surfaces like wet pavement.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: How difficult is braking in a turn?

options.text: Easier than braking on a straightaway.
More difficult than braking on a straightaway.
Done safely by using the front brake only.
Done safely by using the rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than braking on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straightaway. You can use both brakes in a turn, but you must know the proper technique and be very careful.

questions.question: Your body removes about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks
Four drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. In this case, 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals 4 drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: When a motorcyclist carries a passenger, they should tell the passenger to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Hold onto the seat.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger complete safety instructions before riding. Have them get on only after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as comfortable and hold your waist firmly. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: Never
Only during the day
Only at night
Both day and night

questions.correctAnswerText: Both day and night
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times to stay visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket when riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take breaks to remove it and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Riding jackets protect you from overheating and dehydration. Many jackets are designed to keep riders comfortable even in warm weather.

questions.question: What should you do to increase your visibility?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Wear dark clothes.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothing, keep your headlight on all the time, and change your lane position as needed based on conditions.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects your ability to steer.
The front tire powers the bike, so you lose acceleration.
The flat tire shakes the bike, making mirrors hard to use.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects your ability to steer.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it prevents you from steering properly. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely leave the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax on the handgrips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle. Gradually use the brake on the tire that is still good. Move toward the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: What kind of pants should a motorcycle rider wear for protection?

options.text: Soft material
Heavy material
Loose fitting so they flap in the wind
Short pants that expose some leg

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy material
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. Clothing should fit snugly without flapping in the wind, but not so tight that it limits your movement.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective eyewear for motorcycle riding?

options.text: Contact lenses
Glasses
Goggles
A face shield

questions.correctAnswerText: Contact lenses
questions.explanation: Riders must wear protective eyewear such as glasses, goggles, or a face shield. Contact lenses do not count as protective eyewear, even if the motorcycle has a windscreen.

questions.question: What is the problem with riding alongside another motorcyclist?

options.text: It allows you to use more of the road.
It limits your escape routes if you hit a hazard.
It allows you to communicate with each other.
It makes it easier for other drivers to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes if you hit a hazard.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcyclist. This limits both riders' options for escaping if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hand ready on both the clutch and brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.
Drive below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hand ready on both the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hand ready on both the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time needed to react to hazards.

questions.question: What is true about a windshield?

options.text: It works as well as a face shield.
It does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
It is required on all motorcycles.
You should use it only on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from the wind.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Only move your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?

options.text: 10 percent
25 percent
50 percent
75 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 75 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should riders do when changing lanes?

options.text: Only use their mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Ignore other traffic.
Brake hard to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which part of your body operates the gearshift lever?

options.text: Your right hand.
Your right foot.
Your left hand.
Your left foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest and is operated by your left foot.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is considered legally intoxicated?

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What does it mean when a rider extends their left arm straight out?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals when mechanical turn signals are not available. A left arm extended straight out means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen most clearly?

options.text: Orange and red.
Green and blue.
Purple and gold.
Black and white.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up, if possible.
Stay on your seat and lift your feet off the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down. Approach it at a 90-degree angle if you can. Keep your motorcycle upright. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What lane position should riders generally use?

options.text: Always use the same lane position.
Change lane positions often to stay alert.
Choose a position that gives you the most space around your motorcycle.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a position that gives you the most space around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly, so the best lane position changes too. Pick the position that gives you the most space cushion and helps other drivers see you clearly.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the road is slippery.
When there are only a few vehicles on the road.
When the sun is shining.
When drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: A friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Let them.
Tell them to take quiet roads.
Do not get involved.
Take their keys.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take their keys.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have drunk too much. Do what you can to stop them, including taking their keys. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help you avoid an accident?

options.text: Staying alert.
Spotting hazards and deciding which ones to handle first.
Riding without a headlight.
Keeping space around your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, stay alert and be ready to react. Notice hazards and decide which ones need your attention first. Always use your headlight so other drivers can see you. Keep plenty of space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It means the driver sees you.
It does not guarantee the driver will give you the right of way.
It guarantees the driver will give you the right of way.
It may make the driver angry.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the driver will give you the right of way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means a driver will give you the right of way. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still do not see them.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: Far from home.
On short trips.
On long rides.
Several hours into the ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: What is the best source of information for your specific motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual.
A general book about motorcycles.
Someone who owns a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before you ride it for the first time. This is especially important if you are borrowing a motorcycle.

questions.question: Why are brightly-colored helmets helpful?

options.text: They may help other drivers see you.
They can be distracting.
They do not help with visibility.
They are not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may help other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is a good choice. It protects you in a crash and helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: Why should you check your motorcycle before every ride?

options.text: It is only useful if a mechanic does it.
It should not be done before a ride.
It should only be done after a ride.
It can help you spot mechanical problems or broken equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can help you spot mechanical problems or broken equipment.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures that could put you in danger.
